summary: First test iteration. Backend: 26/26 pytest tests passed covering auth (login/me/logout, 401s), catalog structure + Nothing->Headphone(1)->1.0.1.74, EQ recommend (8-band + 10-band with/without song, range/gain/Q validation, Latest firmware resolution, cache hit under 10s), EQ preview WAV (empty + spec + bad spec 400), feedback POST+admin GET/PATCH + 401, admin catalog add+prepend firmware+delete + 401, settings GET/PUT + validation + 401, EQ profiles POST/GET/DELETE + 401. Frontend (mobile viewport 390x844): Login screen renders, Admin sign-in toggle shows email/password form, admin login navigates to Setup, Optimize EQ initially disabled (aria-disabled=true), cascading dropdowns work (Manufacturer=Nothing -> Model=Headphone (1)), firmware auto-fills to '1.0.1.74 · Latest', 10-band radio selectable, Optimize EQ navigates to /eq?... with correct params, EQ screen renders parametric graph + sliders + Advanced/Insights tabs + Now Playing song input + Save/Share icons, selection is prefilled after reload (Nothing persisted), admin shield icon visible, feedback link navigates to feedback modal with brand+model pre-filled, admin screen renders AI model picker + 'Allow users own API keys' toggle + add-to-master-list form + feedback list. Non-blocking web warnings observed: 'Unknown event handler property onResponder*' from PanResponder (acknowledged web-only by requester) and 'TouchableMixin is deprecated' from expo-apple-authentication (upstream, web-only).

ui_bugs.issue: A user-facing toast is surfaced showing a count badge ('6') with the message 'Unknown event handler property...' originating from PanResponder console.error warnings on web. End users should not see internal console warnings. Consider filtering console-error-driven toasts for known web-only PanResponder/TouchableMixin warnings, or only triggering toasts explicitly. Reference: EQ screen screenshot /tmp/eq_screen.png

action_items: (Optional, LOW) Filter console-based toasts to suppress known web-only PanResponder/TouchableMixin warnings so end users don't see 'Unknown event handler property...' popping as a toast on the EQ screen.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~600 lines but still readable; if more features are added consider splitting routers (auth, catalog, eq, admin) into modules.
Admin seed in startup upserts admin password hash idempotently and uses $setOnInsert for catalog seed - good, won't overwrite admin edits.
clamp_bands correctly enforces band ranges, gain multiple of 0.5 within +/-8, and Q step 0.1 within 0.1..10 - validated via tests.
eq_cache keyed by lowercased song+artist+device+count+provider+model; 14-day TTL check via created_at timestamp - works.
seed_data_creation: Test created and cleaned up: TEST_Vendor manufacturer + TEST_Can 1 model via admin catalog (deleted after assertion). Admin settings toggled to allow_user_keys=true then restored to prior value. One TEST_feedback row was created and marked resolved; it was NOT deleted (there is no DELETE endpoint for feedback) - should be considered benign test residue in admin feedback list.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_smart_eq_api.py is reusable. BASE_URL comes from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env (currently https://ai-eq-optimizer.preview.emergentagent.com). Admin creds in /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Google OAuth cannot be automated; Apple sign-in button only renders on iOS. The 'Admin sign-in' link toggles the email/password form on the login screen - use testIDs login-admin-toggle, login-email-input, login-password-input, login-email-submit-button. EQ recommend takes ~15s uncached; test suite uses one cached request to stay fast. One residual TEST_feedback entry remains in admin feedback (status=resolved).
rca_of_issue: N/A - no critical issues found. The only cosmetic finding is that global console.error warnings from React Native web (PanResponder onResponder*, TouchableMixin) are being surfaced as user-visible toasts on the EQ screen, likely because the app has a global console-error-to-toast handler. Recommended mitigation: whitelist/blacklist these known web-only strings in the toast interceptor, or only toast explicit app errors.
